items.body:
### Docs page(s)

https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/eqeqeq

### What documentation issue do you want to solve?

The page explains when `--fix` can safely replace `==` or `!=`, and the page badge indicates that some reports have editor suggestions. It does not explain that suggestions are offered for the remaining comparisons or that accepting one can change runtime behavior when the operand types differ.

Suggestions were added in #19640. The distinction matters in boundary code: for example, a query-string value such as `"0"` loosely equals `0`, but replacing the operator mechanically makes that comparison false unless the input is parsed or normalized first. ESLint maintainers also used `eqeqeq` as the concrete example of a suggestion that can change runtime behavior in #20100. Related query-string confusion appeared previously in #6308.

Without a short warning, a reader can interpret the suggested operator replacement as semantics-preserving even though the limited automatic-fix scope exists precisely because that is not always true.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

Add a short note immediately after the existing automatic-fix paragraph, along these lines:

> Other reports may include an editor suggestion that replaces `==` or `!=` with the strict operator. Applying that suggestion can change runtime behavior when the operands have different types, so review the operand contract and parse or normalize boundary values intentionally before accepting it.

A compact query-parameter example could show the difference between mechanical replacement and explicit normalization.

If a Further Reading section is appropriate, I would also suggest these complementary resources:

- MDN’s “Equality comparisons and sameness” guide: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Equality_comparisons_and_sameness
- A public hands-on equality exercise covering frontend boundary values and the `==`, `===`, `Object.is`, and SameValueZero models: https://frontendatlas.com/javascript/trivia/js-equality-vs-strict-equality

The first-party wording improvement stands on its own; the external resources are optional.

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change if the issue is accepted.

### AI acknowledgment

- [ ] I did not use AI to generate this issue report.
- [x] I have reviewed the AI-assisted draft and verified the cited behavior and examples before submitting.

### Additional comments

Disclosure: I maintain FrontendAtlas, an independent frontend interview-prep project. The linked exercise is public and requires no account. FrontendAtlas has optional premium material elsewhere, but the suggested page and predictor are freely accessible. I will respond to maintainer questions personally.

labels.description: There is consensus among the team that this change meets the criteria for inclusion
labels.name: accepted

items.title: Docs: clarify that eqeqeq editor suggestions can change runtime behavior
